Build an acronym from the first letter of each word of a phrase, treating hyphens as word separators and ignoring other punctuation.

Adapted from Exercism's [problem specification](https://github.com/exercism/problem-specifications/tree/main/exercises/acronym) (MIT). Listed under [Strings & Text](/examples/?subject=strings-and-text).

```nomi-run
// FILE: acronym.nomi
import std/regex.Regex

/// The acronym of `phrase`: the first letter of each word, upper-cased.
/// Hyphens and other punctuation separate words; an apostrophe does not.
pub fn abbreviate(phrase: String) -> String {
    phrase
    |> String.find_all(Regex`[A-Za-z][A-Za-z']*`)
    |> Iter.map(&String.slice(&1, 0, 1))
    |> String.join()
    |> String.to_upper()
}

// FILE: acronym_test.nomi
import acronym.abbreviate

test "abbreviates phrases" {
    cases = [
        #("basic", "Portable Network Graphics", "PNG"),
        #("lowercase words", "Ruby on Rails", "ROR"),
        #("punctuation", "First In, First Out", "FIFO"),
        #("all caps word", "GNU Image Manipulation Program", "GIMP"),
        #("punctuation without whitespace", "Complementary metal-oxide semiconductor", "CMOS"),
        #(
            "very long abbreviation",
            "Rolling On The Floor Laughing So Hard That My Dogs Came Over And Licked Me",
            "ROTFLSHTMDCOALM",
        ),
        #("consecutive delimiters", "Something - I made up from thin air", "SIMUFTA"),
        #("apostrophes", "Halley's Comet", "HC"),
        #("underscore emphasis", "The Road _Not_ Taken", "TRNT"),
    ]

    subtests cases, #(description, phrase, expected), description {
        assert abbreviate(phrase) == expected
    }
}
```

## How it's written

- Words are found with one regex, `[A-Za-z][A-Za-z']*`, through
  `String.find_all`, rather than splitting on spaces and hyphens and then
  stripping punctuation. The regex makes "Halley's" one word and "_Not_" the
  word "Not" without special cases.
- The first letter of a word is `&String.slice(&1, 0, 1)`, a capture rather than `fn word -> ...` (style §31: one call that uses its parameter once).
  `Iter.first(word)` also works but returns a `Maybe`, and every match has at
  least one letter.
- The whole acronym is upper-cased once at the end, not letter by letter.
